lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: David hears of Saul's death and laments
nodes.d: An Amalekite brings David news of Saul's death and claims to have killed him; David has him put to death for slaying the LORD's anointed, and composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David responded to the news that Saul was dead?
ev: Say what the Amalekite claimed and what David did (1:8-16)
Say what David said about Jonathan in his lament (1:26)

nodes.d: 2 Samuel follows David from the news of Saul's death to his kingship over Judah and then all Israel, the LORD's promise of a lasting house, his sin with Bathsheba and its consequences in his own family, Absalom's and Sheba's revolts, and closing songs, warriors and a census.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 2 Samuel from David's lament for Saul to the census at the end?
ev: Say how the book begins and what David did first
Name the promise in chapter 7
Name some consequences in David's family after chapter 11

nodes.t: David made king of Judah; war with Ishbosheth
nodes.d: At Hebron the men of Judah anoint David king, while Abner makes Saul's son Ishbosheth king over the other tribes; a skirmish at Gibeon ends with Asahel killed by Abner.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel was divided between David and Ishbosheth?
ev: Say who anointed David at Hebron (2:4)
Say who Abner made king (2:8-9)
Say what happened to Asahel (2:18-23)

nodes.t: Abner joins David and is killed by Joab
nodes.d: Abner quarrels with Ishbosheth and offers to bring Israel to David; Joab kills Abner in revenge for Asahel, and David publicly mourns him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Abner and what David said about it?
ev: Say why Abner turned to David (3:7-12)
Say what Joab did and how David responded (3:27-39)

nodes.d: Two of Ishbosheth's captains kill him in his bed and bring his head to David, who has them put to death; Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth is introduced.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what David did when Ishbosheth was murdered?
ev: Say what Rechab and Baanah did and how David responded (4:5-12)

nodes.t: David king over all Israel; Jerusalem and the Philistines
nodes.d: The tribes come to Hebron and anoint David king over Israel; he takes Zion and makes it the city of David, Hiram sends help for his house, and David defeats the Philistines twice after inquiring of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?
ev: Say who came to David at Hebron and what they said (5:1-3)
Say what city David took (5:6-9)
Say how David received guidance against the Philistines (5:19, 5:23-25)

nodes.t: David brings the ark to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Uzzah dies when he touches the ark on the cart, so David leaves it at Obed-edom's house; after three months he brings it into the city with sacrifices and dancing, and Michal despises him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark came to Jerusalem?
ev: Say what happened to Uzzah (6:6-7)
Say what happened to Obed-edom's house (6:11)
Say how David and Michal reacted when the ark came in (6:14-16, 6:20-23)

nodes.d: David wishes to build a house for the ark; the LORD sends Nathan to say that he will make David a house, set up his offspring after him, establish his throne for ever, and be a father to his son; David then prays in thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised David through Nathan?
ev: Say what David wanted to do (7:2)
List what the LORD promised David (7:8-16)
Say how David responded (7:18-29)

nodes.d: David subdues the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria and Edom, dedicates silver and gold to the LORD, and reigns over all Israel executing judgment and justice, with a list of officers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of David's victories and say what he did with the silver and gold?
ev: Name some peoples David defeated (8:1-14)
Say what David did with the gifts and spoil (8:11)

nodes.d: David asks if any of Saul's house remains to whom he can show kindness for Jonathan's sake, learns from Ziba of Mephibosheth, restores Saul's land to him, and has him eat at the king's table.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David was kind to Mephibosheth and why?
ev: Say why David sought someone from Saul's house (9:1)
Say what David gave Mephibosheth (9:7, 9:10-13)

nodes.t: The war with Ammon and Syria
nodes.d: David's envoys to the new Ammonite king Hanun are humiliated, so Ammon hires Syrian troops; Joab and Abishai defeat Ammon's allies and David defeats the Syrians again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why David went to war with Ammon and the Syrians?
ev: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (10:4)
Say how the war ended (10:13-19)

nodes.d: While Israel fights at Rabbah, David takes Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, and when Uriah will not go home he has Joab place him where he will be killed, then marries Bathsheba; the text says this displeased the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what David did wrong and how the chapter judges it?
ev: Say what David did and then tried to cover up (11:4, 11:6-15)
Say what Uriah said about the ark and the army (11:11)
Say how the chapter ends (11:27)

nodes.d: Nathan tells David a parable of a rich man and a poor man's lamb and says "Thou art the man"; David confesses, the LORD puts away his sin, but the sword will not leave his house and the child born dies; Solomon is then born.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Nathan showed David his sin and what followed?
ev: Retell Nathan's parable and how David responded (12:1-7)
Say what David confessed and what Nathan answered (12:13)
Say what consequences were announced (12:10-14)
Say who was born to David and Bathsheba next (12:24-25)

nodes.d: David's son Amnon forces his half-sister Tamar and then casts her out; David is angry but Absalom, after two years, has Amnon killed at a feast and flees to Geshur.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened among David's sons Amnon and Absalom?
ev: Say what Amnon did to Tamar (13:11-17)
Say what Absalom did two years later (13:23-29)
Say where Absalom went (13:37-38)

nodes.d: Joab uses a wise woman of Tekoah with a parable to move David to bring Absalom back from Geshur; David lets him return but does not see him for two years, until Absalom forces Joab to arrange a meeting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Absalom came back to Jerusalem?
ev: Say how Joab persuaded David (14:1-21)
Say how long Absalom did not see the king after returning (14:24-28)

nodes.d: Absalom wins the hearts of Israel, has himself proclaimed king at Hebron, and David flees Jerusalem with his servants, sends the ark back, and plants Hushai to oppose Ahithophel; Ziba and Shimei meet him, and Absalom takes David's concubines.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Absalom turned the people against David and how David responded?
ev: Describe how Absalom won the people (15:1-6)
Say what David did with the ark and with Hushai (15:25-37)
Say how David answered Shimei's cursing (16:10-12)

nodes.d: Ahithophel advises Absalom to pursue David at once, but Hushai persuades him to wait and gather all Israel because the LORD had appointed to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel; messengers warn David, who crosses the Jordan, and Ahithophel hangs himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hushai's advice saved David?
ev: Say what each counsellor advised (17:1-13)
Say why Absalom chose Hushai's advice (17:14)
Say what David received at Mahanaim (17:27-29)

nodes.d: David's army meets Absalom's in the wood of Ephraim; Absalom's head is caught in an oak and Joab kills him despite David's order to deal gently, and David weeps, "O my son Absalom".
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Absalom died and how David reacted?
ev: Say what David ordered about Absalom (18:5)
Say how Absalom died (18:9-15)
Say how David reacted to the news (18:33)

nodes.d: Joab rebukes David's grief for Absalom; David returns toward Jerusalem, spares Shimei, hears Mephibosheth's account and divides the land between him and Ziba, honours Barzillai, and Israel and Judah quarrel over the king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how David came back as king after Absalom's death?
ev: Say what Joab told David (19:5-7)
Say what David did to Shimei (19:23)
Say what Barzillai asked and what David did (19:31-39)

nodes.t: Sheba's revolt and Joab kills Amasa
nodes.d: Sheba the Benjamite calls Israel to leave David; Joab kills Amasa and pursues Sheba to Abel, where a wise woman persuades the city to throw out Sheba's head.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Sheba's revolt ended?
ev: Say what Sheba proclaimed (20:1)
Say what happened to Amasa (20:8-10)
Say what the wise woman of Abel did (20:16-22)

nodes.d: A three-year famine comes, and the LORD says it is because Saul put the Gibeonites to death; at the Gibeonites' request seven of Saul's sons are hanged, Mephibosheth is spared for the sake of the oath with Jonathan, and Saul's and Jonathan's bones are buried in Kish's tomb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the famine came and what David did about it?
ev: Say what the LORD said was the cause of the famine (21:1)
Say why Mephibosheth was spared (21:7)
Say what David did with the bones of Saul and Jonathan (21:12-14)

nodes.d: Several descendants of the giant, including a brother of Goliath, are slain in battles at Gob and Gath by David's men after David grows faint.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some of David's men who defeated the Philistine giants?
ev: Say who rescued David when he grew faint (21:15-17)
Say who killed the brother of Goliath (21:19)

nodes.d: David praises the LORD as rock, fortress and deliverer who answered his cry, rescued him from his enemies and Saul, and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and his seed for evermore.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what David praises the LORD for in this song?
ev: Say the titles David gives the LORD (22:2-3)
Describe how the LORD answered David's cry (22:7-20)
Say what the song says about David's seed (22:51)

nodes.t: David's last words and the everlasting covenant
nodes.d: In his last words David says the Spirit of the LORD spoke by him that a ruler must be just and rule in the fear of God, and that although his house is not so with God, the LORD has made with him an everlasting covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what David says about God's covenant with him in his last words?
ev: Say what David says a ruler must be (23:3)
Say how David describes his covenant with God (23:5)

nodes.d: The chapter lists David's mighty men and their deeds, including the three who fetched water from the well of Bethlehem, which David poured out to the LORD instead of drinking.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did with the water from Bethlehem's well?
ev: Say what the three mighty men did for David (23:15-16)
Say what David did with the water (23:16-17)

nodes.t: David's census and the threshing floor
nodes.d: David has Joab count Israel despite Joab's protest and afterward confesses he has sinned; the LORD gives him a choice of three punishments, a plague strikes Israel, and David buys Araunah's threshing floor and builds an altar, whereupon the plague is stayed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did wrong in chapter 24 and how it ended?
ev: Say what David did and how he felt afterward (24:2, 24:10)
Say which punishment David chose (24:14)
Say what David did at Araunah's threshing floor (24:24-25)

nodes.d: The people of Gibeon pretend to come from a far country and trick Israel into a treaty without asking the LORD; when found out, they are made woodcutters and water carriers and spared because of the oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Gibeonites tricked Joshua and what happened next?
ev: Retell how Gibeon deceived Israel
Say what Israel failed to do (9:14)
Explain why Israel did not destroy them (9:18-21)

nodes.d: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?
ev: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)

nodes.t: The ark comes back to Israel
nodes.d: The Philistines send the ark home on a cart pulled by two cows with a trespass offering; the cows go straight to Beth-shemesh, where seventy men are struck for looking into the ark, and the ark is taken to Kirjath-jearim.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the ark went back to Israel?
ev: Say what the Philistines sent with the ark (6:4-8)
Say what the cows did (6:12)
Say what happened at Beth-shemesh (6:19-21)

nodes.d: Goliath of Gath defies Israel for forty days; David, sent with food for his brothers, volunteers, refuses Saul's armour, and in the name of the LORD of hosts kills Goliath with a sling and stone, saying the battle is the LORD's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of David and Goliath and who David trusted?
ev: Retell how David came to fight Goliath
Say what David told Goliath about the LORD (17:45-47)
Say how David killed Goliath (17:48-51)

nodes.d: David asks Jonathan to find out Saul's intent; Saul's anger at the new moon feast confirms he wants David dead, and Jonathan signals this with arrows, before the friends part in tears after renewing their oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jonathan warned David with the arrows?
ev: Say how Jonathan and David planned to learn Saul's mind (20:5-23)
Say what Saul did to Jonathan at the feast (20:30-34)
Say what the two friends swore at parting (20:42)

nodes.t: The death of Saul and his sons
nodes.d: Israel flees before the Philistines at Mount Gilboa; Jonathan and two brothers are killed, Saul takes his own life after being wounded, and the men of Jabesh-gilead recover and bury the bodies.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Saul and Jonathan died?
ev: Say who died at Gilboa
Say what the men of Jabesh-gilead did (31:11-13)

nodes.t: God has spoken by his Son
nodes.d: God who spoke by the prophets has in these last days spoken by his Son, heir of all things, maker of the worlds, radiance of his glory, who purged sins and sat at God's right hand, better than the angels.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 1:1-4 says about how God has spoken and who the Son is?
ev: List what 1:2-3 says about the Son
Say how 1:4-14 compares him with angels

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)
